body:
### Summary

Hi,

this issue was already reported here:

https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/20567

but that issue was closed as "a duplicate" of issue:

https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/20792

But when I explained the exact mechanism of the problem, I was told that this issue is about AV holding exclusive locks - which is not the case in this particular instance. For convenience, here is my comment on that issue:

> We are currently facing this issue (BitDefender GravityZone) and it is causing me endless grief, so I decided to look into it a bit. In my understanding, the main cause of the issue is that when uv writes the PE resources to the trampoline it does a write_resource (https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/main/crates/uv-trampoline-builder/src/lib.rs#L479) which does an EndUpdateResourceW (https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/main/crates/uv-trampoline-builder/src/lib.rs#L317). This call re-opens the file for reading and writing without resource sharing. It essentially requests full, exclusive access to an executable file it just wrote. Do you see how AV software might have a problem with that?
>
>Our IT department will contact BitDefender, but after looking into it, I think this is not an issue to be fixed on the side of the AV vendors, because that software is just doing its job. By creating an executable file and then "trying to prevent other processes from opening it" (I know this is not the intent, but that's how it looks to the AV software) uv is kind of overstaying its welcome.
>
>This was the first time I looked at the uv source and I'm only a beginner at Rust, so I couldn't really tell you how to solve the issue but I would really appreciate it if someone more knowledgeable could look into it. If I'm completely wrong about this, I'd also appreciate it if you told me why.
>
>Thank you very much for working on uv which is one of my favorite development tools. You guys rule!
>
>(Full disclosure: the investigation was performed with the help of AI tools. I did not use AI to write this post and I made sure I understood and validated the findings as per your AI policy)

Just to stress this: the AV is not holding exclusive locks. My tests show that it is not actually holding any lock. It is actively injecting the exception because what uv is doing is considered dangerous. As far as I understand, there is no reason to close the file and re-open it. I think I even saw a comment in the code somewhere that this behavior was weird.

I'd really appreciate it if you could take the time to look into this.

### Platform

Windows 11

### Version

0.11.28 (ebf0f43d7 2026-07-07 x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)

### Python version

Any, but only those managed by uv are affected
title: uv tries to open recently written trampoline executable for exclusive access, flagged by AV
